# Track & Trace ontology tutorial part 1: Create an ontology

In this step of the tutorial, you create a new ontology (preview) item that represents the Track & Trace
scenario. Then you add entity types, data bindings and relationship types to build out the ontology.

## Create ontology (preview) item

1. In your Fabric workspace, select **+ New item**.
1. Search for and select the **Ontology (preview)** item.
1. In the **New Ontology** dialog, enter a **Name** of *TrackTraceOntology*. Set the **Location** to your
   workspace and select **Create**. The ontology opens when it's ready.

> [!NOTE]
> If Fabric can't create the ontology (preview) item, make sure the tenant settings from the
> [part 0 prerequisites](tutorial-0-introduction.md#prerequisites) are enabled.

Next, create entity types, data bindings and relationship types based on the data in your lakehouse,
eventhouse and semantic model.

## Create entity types and data bindings

Entity types represent the types of objects in the business: a factory, a pack, a shipment. After you create an
entity type, create its properties by binding source data columns from the **TrackTraceLH** lakehouse tables.

### Property names

Two source columns appear in several tables with a different meaning each time: `name` and `status`. Give them
an entity-specific property name when you bind data, as the Learn tutorial does with *LocationName*. Distinct
names keep their descriptions apart in part 2 and make agent answers easier to read. The table in
[Add other entity types](#add-other-entity-types) lists each renamed property.

Other shared columns, such as `line_id`, `sku`, `order_id` or `shipment_id`, mean the same thing in every table.
If a property already exists, select its name from the property name dropdown menu to reuse it instead of
creating a duplicate.

### Add base entity type (Warehouse)

1. On the **Home** tab of the top ribbon, select **+ Add > Entity type**.
1. Enter *Warehouse* for the entity type name and select **Add**. The Warehouse entity type appears on the
   configuration canvas.

### Bind Warehouse data

1. On the configuration canvas or the **Explorer**, select **...** next to the entity name and select
   **Bind data**.
1. Select the plus (**+**) button next to **Data sources**, and then select **OneLake catalog**.
1. Expand **TrackTraceLH > Schemas > dbo** and select the **warehouse** table. Confirm with **Select**. The data
   source loads.
1. Select **Properties** under **Entity type**. The columns of the warehouse table populate as proposed
   properties.
1. Review the proposed properties. Use *warehouse_name* as the property name for the **name** source column.
1. Select **Create** to save the data binding and return to the **Configure** page. It shows the entity type's
   properties and data bindings.

Now the Warehouse entity type is complete.

### Add inherited entity type (Distributor)

Distributors and hubs are both warehouses. Next, add an inherited entity type: Distributor inherits from
Warehouse, which automatically gives it all of Warehouse's properties.

1. Select **Home** in the breadcrumb above the **Configure** tab to return to the configuration canvas.
1. On the **Home** tab of the top ribbon, select **+ Add > Entity type**.
1. Enter *Distributor* for the **Entity type name**. Expand **Additional configuration** and set
   **Choose entity to inherit from (optional)** to **Warehouse**. Select **Add**.
1. Select the Distributor entity type and select **Entity type > Open details**. In the **Configure** tab,
   confirm that Distributor already has properties. They're inherited from Warehouse, but you still need to bind
   them to a source.

### Bind Distributor data

1. Select **Bind data**. The **Bind data** page opens.
1. Select the plus (**+**) button next to **Data sources**, and then select **OneLake catalog**.
1. Expand **TrackTraceLH > Schemas > dbo**, select **warehouse**, and then select **Select**.
1. Select **Properties** under **Entity type**, and map the inherited properties to their source columns.
   Inherited property names and types are read-only; use the **Source column** selectors to set their bindings.
1. Verify that *warehouse_name* maps to **warehouse.name**, and select **Create**.

Now the Distributor entity type is complete. In part 2 you describe it as the warehouses where
`warehouse_type = DISTRIBUTOR`.

### Add other entity types

Start each entity type with **Home > + Add > Entity type**, and follow the same steps that you used for
Warehouse and Distributor to create the entity types in the following table. Add all of their source columns as
properties.

| Entity type name | Inherits from | Data source table | Property name changes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hub | Warehouse | TrackTraceLH > warehouse | (inherited) | |
| Factory | | TrackTraceLH > factory | name → *factory_name* | |
| Production Line | | TrackTraceLH > production_line | status → *line_status* | |
| Production Order | | TrackTraceLH > production_order | status → *order_status* | |
| Product | | TrackTraceLH > product | | |
| Cigarette | Product | TrackTraceLH > product | (inherited) | |
| Heated Tobacco Stick | Product | TrackTraceLH > product | (inherited) | |
| Pack | | TrackTraceLH > pack | status → *pack_status* | The largest table; packs exist for production from 20 November 2026 |
| Bundle | | TrackTraceLH > bundle | status → *bundle_status* | |
| Shipping Case | | TrackTraceLH > shipping_case | | |
| Pallet | | TrackTraceLH > pallet | status → *pallet_status* | |
| Shipment | | TrackTraceLH > shipment | status → *shipment_status* | |
| Market | | TrackTraceLH > market | name → *market_name* | |
| Tax Authority | | TrackTraceLH > tax_authority | name → *authority_name* | |
| Authority Submission | | TrackTraceLH > authority_submission | status → *submission_status* | |
| Partner | | TrackTraceLH > partner | name → *partner_name* | Carriers, a 3PL and a customs broker |
| Inventory Position | | TrackTraceLH > inventory_snapshot | | |
| Demand Forecast | | TrackTraceLH > demand_forecast | | |
| Maintenance Event | | TrackTraceLH > maintenance_log | | |
| Consumer Scan | | TrackTraceLH > consumer_scan | | |
| Trace Event | | TrackTraceEH > TraceEvent | | This entity type uses the eventhouse table, not a lakehouse table, as its data source. |
| Scanner Telemetry | | TrackTraceEH > LineScannerTelemetry | | Eventhouse table, like Trace Event. |

When you finish, you see all the entity types listed in the **Explorer** in the configuration canvas.

### Add Line Production Day with the ontology agent

Finally, add one more entity type: Line Production Day. Unlike the other entity types, its source data is in a
semantic model and has DAX measures. To bind this data without recreating it manually, use the ontology agent.

1. Select **Home > Ontology agent** from the ribbon. The ontology agent opens in **Plan** mode.
1. Send the following query:

   > Create a new entity type called Line Production Day, bound to data in the ProductionDaily table from the
   > TrackTraceKPIs semantic model inside this workspace.

   The ontology agent reasons and creates a plan for adding the new entity type.
1. Toggle to **Act** mode and send *Apply the entity type plan*. The ontology agent adds the Line Production Day
   entity type to the canvas.
1. With Line Production Day highlighted, select **Entity type > Open details**. Verify that **Properties** are
   populated and bound to the semantic model data source.
1. Scroll down to the **Metrics** section and verify that three metrics are added: **Packs Commissioned**,
   **Aggregation Error Rate %** and **Plan Attainment %**. Ontology metrics are based on the DAX measures of the
   semantic model.

Now you have all entity types for the scenario created and bound to source data.

> [!NOTE]
> At the time of writing, Learn lists a known issue: a Fabric data agent doesn't work with an ontology that uses
> semantic models for binding. That doesn't affect parts 1 to 4. Part 5 shows how to handle it for the demo
> agents.

## Create relationship types

Next, create relationship types between the entity types to represent the connections in your data. The first
one connects a pallet to the shipment it travels with.

### Pallet loadedOn Shipment

1. Select the **Pallet** entity type in the **Explorer**.
1. On the **Home** tab of the top ribbon, select **+ Add > Relationship type**. With Pallet selected, you can
   also select **Entity type > + Add > Relationship type**.
1. Enter the following relationship type details and select **Add**:
   - **Name**: *loadedOn*
   - **Origin entity type**: Pallet
   - **Target entity type**: Shipment

   The relationship appears on the canvas. Select it to open the relationship details configuration.
1. Observe the sections of the configuration page: **Origin entity type** (Pallet), **Relationship name**
   (loadedOn), **Target entity type** (Shipment), and the **Use mapping table** switch.
1. In the **Origin entity type** section, expand **Property 1** and select **shipment_id**.
1. In the **Target entity type** section, expand **Property 1** and select **shipment_id**. These fields indicate
   that the shipment_id on a pallet matches the shipment_id of a shipment.
1. Save the relationship type. You see a banner confirming that the ontology successfully updated the
   relationship type. Select **Cancel** to close the configuration options.

You see the Configure page of the Pallet entity type, with the new relationship in the **Relationships**
section. Now the first relationship is complete.

> [!TIP]
> **Mapping tables and the graph.** In part 3 you project part of the ontology into a graph, and the graph needs
> each relationship to have a data binding with a single backing table. If you plan to do part 3, turn on
> **Use mapping table** instead of setting Property 1 directly: select the key property of each entity type
> (Pallet: *pallet_uid*, Shipment: *shipment_id*), choose the mapping table **TrackTraceLH > pallet** from the
> OneLake catalog, and match its **pallet_uid** and **shipment_id** columns. The last column of the tables below
> lists the mapping table for each relationship. You can also add mapping tables later, in part 3.

### Add other relationship types

Select **Home** in the breadcrumb to return to the configuration canvas. On the **Home** tab of the ribbon,
select **+ Add > Relationship type** to add each relationship type. Follow the same steps that you used for
loadedOn to create the relationship types in the following tables.

In the last column, the first mapping column matches the key of the origin entity type and the second matches
the key of the target entity type.

**Needed for the storyline:**

| Relationship type name | Origin entity type (Property) | Target entity type (Property) | Mapping table (columns) |
|---|---|---|---|
| hasLine | Factory (factory_id) | Production Line (factory_id) | production_line (factory_id, line_id) |
| runsOrder | Production Line (line_id) | Production Order (line_id) | production_order (line_id, order_id) |
| producesProduct | Production Order (sku) | Product (sku) | production_order (order_id, sku) |
| commissionedUnder | Pack (order_id) | Production Order (order_id) | pack (pack_uid, order_id) |
| aggregatedIntoBundle | Pack (bundle_uid) | Bundle (bundle_uid) | pack (pack_uid, bundle_uid) |
| aggregatedIntoCase | Bundle (case_uid) | Shipping Case (case_uid) | bundle (bundle_uid, case_uid) |
| aggregatedIntoPallet | Shipping Case (pallet_uid) | Pallet (pallet_uid) | shipping_case (case_uid, pallet_uid) |
| caseProducedUnder | Shipping Case (order_id) | Production Order (order_id) | shipping_case (case_uid, order_id) |
| loadedOn | Pallet (shipment_id) | Shipment (shipment_id) | pallet (pallet_uid, shipment_id) |
| originatesAt | Shipment (from_location) | Factory (factory_id) | shipment (shipment_id, from_location) |
| deliversTo | Shipment (to_location) | Warehouse (warehouse_id) | shipment (shipment_id, to_location) |
| carriedBy | Shipment (partner_id) | Partner (partner_id) | shipment (shipment_id, partner_id) |
| locatedIn | Warehouse (market_id) | Market (market_id) | warehouse (warehouse_id, market_id) |
| reportsShipment | Authority Submission (shipment_id) | Shipment (shipment_id) | authority_submission (submission_id, shipment_id) |
| submittedTo | Authority Submission (authority_id) | Tax Authority (authority_id) | authority_submission (submission_id, authority_id) |
| stockedAt | Inventory Position (warehouse_id) | Warehouse (warehouse_id) | inventory_snapshot (snapshot_id, warehouse_id) |
| stockOfProduct | Inventory Position (sku) | Product (sku) | inventory_snapshot (snapshot_id, sku) |
| forecastForMarket | Demand Forecast (market_id) | Market (market_id) | demand_forecast (forecast_id, market_id) |
| forecastForProduct | Demand Forecast (sku) | Product (sku) | demand_forecast (forecast_id, sku) |
| loggedOn | Maintenance Event (line_id) | Production Line (line_id) | maintenance_log (log_id, line_id) |
| hasScannerReading | Production Line (line_id) | Scanner Telemetry (line_id) | none (eventhouse, not projected) |
| hasTraceEvent | Pack (pack_uid) | Trace Event (object_uid) | none (eventhouse, not projected) |
| measuredOn | Line Production Day (line_id) | Production Line (line_id) | none (semantic model, not projected) |

**Extra context (optional):**

| Relationship type name | Origin entity type (Property) | Target entity type (Property) | Mapping table (columns) |
|---|---|---|---|
| targetsMarket | Production Order (target_market_id) | Market (market_id) | production_order (order_id, target_market_id) |
| packOfProduct | Pack (sku) | Product (sku) | pack (pack_uid, sku) |
| regulates | Tax Authority (market_id) | Market (market_id) | tax_authority (authority_id, market_id) |
| scanOfPack | Consumer Scan (pack_uid) | Pack (pack_uid) | consumer_scan (scan_id, pack_uid) |
| hasBundleEvent | Bundle (bundle_uid) | Trace Event (object_uid) | none |
| hasCaseEvent | Shipping Case (case_uid) | Trace Event (object_uid) | none |
| hasPalletEvent | Pallet (pallet_uid) | Trace Event (object_uid) | none |

> [!NOTE]
> Keep relationship type names unique. Learn lists a known issue with duplicate relationship names, which is why
> the trace event relationships of bundles, cases and pallets have their own names.

When you're done, the relationship types are visible on the configuration canvas.

## Next steps

In this step, you created an ontology (preview) item and populated it with entity types, their properties, and
relationship types between them. Next, enrich the entity types with more detail:
[Enrich the ontology](tutorial-2-enrich-ontology.md).
